requirements.text: create an HR case for this tax inquiry with priority set to low since it's not urgent, use COE type as Payroll, set the account number as PAYROLL-JM-2025 with account type checking
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND opened_for = 13 AND priority = 'low' AND coe_type = 'Payroll' AND account_number = 'PAYROLL-JM-2025' AND account_type = 'checking' AND short_description LIKE '%tax%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (hr_case_id 61 after 60)

opened_for is Jonathan Martinez's hr_profile 13 (user 13, the only Jonathan Martinez; the benchmark check uses 13); the seed lists his position as IT Support, not the request's Administration (Zachary Martinez, user 93, is the Administration one), and the unique name decides it
priority low as the request states; the benchmark check accepts any of five valid priorities
short_description LIKE '%tax%' kept from the benchmark check; the request calls it a tax inquiry but fixes no wording
account_type checking is a seed value of hr_case.account_type (checking, savings, other)

opened_by not tested: the request does not say who submitted the case; source and hr_service not tested: neither is stated and no tool lists services (the seed's 'Complete Tax Forms through CIC Plus', service 28, is not named)

the task's status, group, assignee and short description are not stated and not tested

matched on the request's spelling 'W-2'
disagreement: expected: A equals 1, B greater_than 0; chose equals 1 because the brief fixes a created row's expected count at 1; an agent that splits the W-2 item into two rows would fail it

assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (notification_id 61 after 60); the only notification the request creates

status draft from 'draft Jonathan a notification'; type update from 'as an update'; both are seed values

Valid Priority Value Verification.evidence: the check accepts any of five priorities; the request says 'priority set to low', so the requirement tests low only (its description's 'standard' value is not in this request)

Task Creation Verification.evidence: its query is identical to Valid Task Type Verification's; the checklist-task requirement carries both, named in its source (its description's 'skip task creation' is not in this request). disagreement: A excluded it as a duplicate, B kept; chose kept because an exact-duplicate check whose cells are all carried is kept jointly

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every id (case 61 for profile 13, task 150, two checklist items selected by wording, notification 61 to the work email) and every value but one. disagreement: Task Creation Verification: A excluded (duplicate query), B kept; chose kept, carried jointly with Valid Task Type Verification by the checklist-task requirement (logged in its evidence). disagreement: the two checklist items' expected count: A equals 1, B greater_than 0; chose equals 1 because a created row's expected count is 1 (logged in each requirement). disagreement: B's stay requirement that no notification go to Jonathan's personal address; dropped because the notification is anchored by id with the work email as a cell, so a wrong address fails the create directly, and the request specifies the address rather than forbidding another: no selector has a boundary here. No stay requirements: every row is anchored by id or selected under the new task's id, and the request forbids nothing. The check named 'Notification draft to Joanne ' (trailing space in the name, 'Joanne' in the description) tests Jonathan Martinez's email, which is right; the name is kept verbatim as the key. Four check descriptions describe a different request (an invalid 'standard' priority, a 'tax_form' type, a Payroll Admin group, skipping task creation); their queries fit this request, so the queries are what was mapped. The checklist seed rows carry today's created_at, which suggests the seed was touched; id_conventions still match (90 rows, highest 90).
